summary.text: Josh Harder is the Democratic incumbent for California's 9th Congressional District, which is centered on San Joaquin County. A Central Valley native with a background in venture capital and consulting, he was first elected to the House in 2018. He serves on the Appropriations Committee and is running for re-election focused on lowering costs, health care and water issues.

paragraphs.text: Born August 1, 1986 in Turlock, California. According to his House website, his family has been in San Joaquin County for five generations, since his great-great-grandfather started a peach farm in Manteca.
Graduated from Modesto High School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Stanford University in 2008.
Earned master's degrees in business administration and public policy from Harvard University in 2014.

Worked as a consultant with The Boston Consulting Group (per Ballotpedia). Wikipedia reports that Bessemer Venture Partners hired him in its New York office in 2014 and that he became a vice president in San Francisco two years later.
Left Bessemer in 2017 to run for Congress, returned to the Central Valley, and taught business at Modesto Junior College.
Won the 2018 general election for California's 10th District by defeating Republican incumbent Jeff Denham, and took office in January 2019.
Re-elected in 2020 (10th District), and in 2022 and 2024 in the redrawn 9th District, defeating Tom Patti in 2022 and Kevin Lincoln in 2024.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Labor-HHS-Education and Interior-Environment subcommittees); his office says he is the first Democratic member from the Central Valley on the committee in almost 50 years. Wikipedia lists him as a vice chair of the New Democrat Coalition.
According to his House website, he lives in Tracy with his wife Pam and their daughters Lillian and Karina.
